title: one-pager-cloud-connector-value-claims-and-gating-checklist
summary: Working one-pager and technical gating checklist for listing a cloud connector integration (beta) in AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces. Includes micro-copy variants for tiles, a minimal acceptance matrix, required artifacts, and open questions for legal/engineering.
content:
Objective: create a concise, deployable one-pager + acceptance checklist that partner-sourced cloud connector integrations (SaaS -> Redwood Dedicated / Private) can use to prepare marketplace listings and required technical gating artifacts. This doc is a working draft — intended to be copy-paste friendly for partner-facing intake and internal acceptance review.

Quick context / why: partners keep asking for a single artifact they can send to us that contains marketing copy, technical manifest, and the minimal security/compliance checklist. We want to (1) speed partner readiness, (2) reduce back-and-forth, and (3) keep listing quality consistent across AWS/Azure/GCP.

1) Tile copy (short-first, then two variants). Pick one per market listing.
- Tagline (10–12 words): "Low-latency LLM inference for your app — scalable, private, and cost-aware."
- 80 char summary (for marketplace hero): "Ship LLM features faster with predictable latency, autoscale, and private deployment options."
- 150 char blurb (search/snippet): "Redwood Inference runs high-performance LLM inference in hosted, dedicated, or private modes. Reduce token cost with caching and quantization profiles."
- 300 char product description (detailed): "Redwood Inference delivers a production-grade inference platform for developers: hosted APIs for quick iteration, reserved dedicated GPU pools for predictable throughput, and VPC/on-prem private deployments for regulated workloads. Built-in routing, caching, and rollout controls keep models reliable while optimizing unit economics."

Copy variant A (developer-focused):
- Headline: "Ship LLM features without re-architecting your infra"
- 120 char: "Integrate via REST/SDK, get predictable latency, and scale with reserved GPU pools when you need them."

Copy variant B (enterprise/security-focused):
- Headline: "Private deployments, audited operators, enterprise SLAs"
- 120 char: "Bring inference into your VPC or on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and rollout controls."

2) Acceptance matrix (minimal column list; each row = requirement). Use these as gating checkpoints for the listing team and partner engineers.
- Required metadata: partner name, connector name, contact email, support SLA (SLA tier), short product description (<=300 chars), marketing logo (512px min, transparent preferred), icon (64px), screenshots (2–4), short demo video (optional).
- Technical manifest: supported APIs (REST/SDK), example request/response, sample latency numbers (p95 1k tokens), max tokens supported, model compatibility list (open models + Redwood-verified).
- Security/compliance: data flow diagram (must show where PII is stored), KMS/HSM usage (yes/no), SOC2 or ISO attestation (if available), customer data retention policy.
- Operational readiness: runbook for incident escalation (email + pager), expected throughput profile (qps), required GPU types for dedicated deployment (e.g., A100, H100), autoscaling safety thresholds.
- Legal & commercial: EULA / reseller terms, pricing metric (per-token / per-embed rates), billing contact, marketplace SKU mapping.

For each row above use status values: "Provided" | "Partial" | "Missing". Internal note: intake form should map these to 0/1/2 for automation in the listing tracker.

3) Minimal artifacts checklist (deliverables partner must upload):
- [ ] Product tile copy (use one of the variants above)
- [ ] 300-char product description (final)
- [ ] Marketing assets (logo, icon, 2 screenshots)
- [ ] Technical manifest (openapi or swagger stub + example requests)
- [ ] Latency/throughput benchmarks (doc with measurement methodology)
- [ ] Security questionnaire answers (PDF)
- [ ] Data processing addendum or pointer to privacy policy
- [ ] Support contact & escalation matrix
- [ ] Pricing proposal (SKU mapping)
- [ ] Legal contact for marketplace agreements

4) Sample intake email / outreach snippet (for partner-facing onboarding):
"Hi <Partner>,
Thanks for partnering — to accelerate listing we need the artifacts below. Please upload them to the shared intake folder or reply to this thread with attachments. After we confirm the manifest and security docs, the marketplace team will schedule a 30-minute tech review.
Required: product tile copy, logo, technical manifest, latency benchmarks, security questionnaire. Optional but helpful: demo video, customer case study."

5) Notes for the internal review committee (short checklist):
- Content review: Is the tile copy accurate and non-misleading? Any regulatory claims (PHI/PIMS) need legal review.
- Security review: Does the data flow diagram show any persistent customer PII in Redwood-hosted caches? If yes, flag for SRE + security.
- Performance review: Do the latency numbers reflect the specific deployment model (hosted vs dedicated vs private)? If partner claims p95 < 200ms for 2k tokens, request replication steps.
- Pricing & SKU mapping: Confirm pricing unit (per-token vs monthly reserved); ensure SKU maps to internal metering keys.

6) Suggested lightweight QA testcases (dev-focused):
- Smoke: 5 concurrent requests with 512 token prompts, measure p95 and error rate <1%
- Edge: Token-length spike (3x usual) to validate KV cache behavior
- Fallback: Simulate a model-restart and ensure client error mode is graceful with documented retry headers
- Security: Verify that API keys do not appear in logs via synthetic request with known key string

7) Open questions (action items):
- Legal: Do we require partners to sign Redwood's DPA for all marketplace listings or only for Private deployments? (owner: @Riley)
- Engineering: For dedicated-only connectors, what is the minimal supported GPU family we can certify? (owner: @Miguel)
- GTM: Should co-marketing be a checkbox in intake or negotiated after listing? prefer checkbox for automation.

8) Minimal timeline for a standard partner listing (estimate):
- Partner assembles artifacts: 3–7 business days
- Technical review (one session + follow-ups): 3–5 business days
- Security review + legal signoff: 5–10 business days (depends on DPA)
- Marketplace submission & publisher review (cloud vendor dependent): 7–21 business days
Total: 18–43 business days (median ~28) — set partner expectations accordingly.

9) Implementation notes / next steps (to-do for internal owner):
- Convert acceptance matrix into a Google Form that maps to JIRA tickets (automation: assign statuses and labels).
- Create a marketplace tile template in Figma with the three copy slots prefilled.
- Draft a short DPA pointer for marketplace listings (ask Legal to approve a redlined pointer).

Notes to self: keep the intro short — partners skim. Use bullet-first approach and link to full technical spec. When in doubt, ask engineering for a 15-minute repro that we can run in our sandbox.

References / links (working):
- Intake form prototype: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/marketplace-intake-proto
- Internal listing tracker board: JIRA-MLP-LISTINGS
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CONNECTOR-ONBOARD-3412
